subject: Post-demo: Request/response log redaction acceptance criteria & next steps
messages:

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Request/response log redaction acceptance criteria & next steps

Hi Asha / Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete asks we captured for MediaCorp's security & privacy team: 

- Scope: Request and response logging for inference endpoints (API front-door + internal service-to-service calls).
- Must remove or render-irreversible any trace tokens / trace IDs before logs leave the customer VPC.
- PII handling: user identifiers (email, phone, national IDs) must be pseudonymized or removed; free-form fields should be scanned and either redacted or flagged for manual review.
- Retention: default 90 days for full logs, aggregated metrics retained longer (TBD).
- Residency: logs for EU customers must remain in EU cloud regions; no egress to US for raw traces.
- Deliverables from Redwood: sample sanitized log file, proposed acceptance criteria checklist for redaction, and a short pilot timeline (2–3 weeks).

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Asha: please send a small sample of the raw logs (we discussed up to 1MB) or a redacted sample if you can't share raw.
2) Neha: we will prepare a short 'redaction acceptance checklist' + a playbook draft on how we implement trace token suppression and header scrubbing.
3) Lauren: I'll loop you in for the pilot run and to map operational responsibilities (who on your side verifies the samples).

I've attached a one-page capture from our demo showing where request/response logs are emitted and the toggle points for automatic scrubbing. Happy to jump on a call if you'd prefer a walkthrough.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Request/response log redaction acceptance criteria & next steps

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. Attaching a sanitized sample of the logs we typically collect (we left in a couple of placeholder IDs so you can see the shape).

A few clarifications from our security team: 
- Trace tokens: these are attached as X-Trace-Token and in some cases show up in query parameters. Our requirement is that any token that could be used to re-identify or replay must not be present in the long-term logs. We prefer complete removal; if you must store a derived value, it should be a one-way hash with salt controlled by MediaCorp.
- Headers: cookies and authorization headers must be omitted entirely. Host and path are fine.
- Pseudonymization: user_id can be replaced with a consistent pseudonym per user for analytics, but salted hashing must be supported (we will provide KMS details later).
- Retention: 90 days for full request/response, 13 months aggregated metrics.

Attached: mediacorp_sample_logs_redacted.csv (small subset). We can't share raw logs externally; this should be enough for a functional test. Also include a link to our SOC contact if you need further details.

Asha
Asha Patel
Sr. Security Engineer — MediaCorp

Thanks Asha — got the sample. I pulled a quick draft acceptance checklist and alignment notes below (we'll convert to a formal doc):

Redaction & Acceptance Checklist (Draft)
- No trace tokens present in retained logs (scanning rule: regex for X-Trace-Token and common trace formats). PASS/FAIL
- Authorization headers removed from stored logs. PASS/FAIL
- Cookies removed from stored logs. PASS/FAIL
- User identifiers pseudonymized with customer-provided salt or using Redwood KMS with per-customer key; ensure determinism for analytics. PASS/FAIL
- Requests containing PII in free-form fields flagged for manual review; auto-redact rules applied for SSN, credit card, email patterns. PASS/FAIL
- Log residency: verified storage region is EU (we will produce a signed manifest of storage location). PASS/FAIL
- Retention policy: retention cycle applied and older logs auto-deleted after 90 days. PASS/FAIL

Proposed pilot plan (2 weeks):
- Day 1: Redwood ingests sanitized sample and runs detection rules; exchange of sample evidence (hashes of output).
- Day 3–5: Redwood implements header/trace suppression in a sandbox and provides a sanitized output for MediaCorp review.
- Day 7: Joint review call to verify PASS/FAIL checklist items.
- Day 10–14: Finalize deployment plan and operational runbooks; schedule go-live.

I'll attach the playbook draft (redaction_playbook_v0.md) to this thread. Once Karthik confirms, I'll own the internal engineering kickoff and loop in runtime.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

We will aim for the pilot kickoff on Mon Aug 5. Neha, please confirm availability for the dev kickoff and whether you need a dedicated ingest endpoint or can accept the sample via the Drive link.

Karthik
